fronts.gap: Gap: from Gaza (about MR 102.4-100.1) to the Egyptian frontier the line is not drawn. Art. VI.1 says only 'continuing thus to the Egyptian frontier' and no map of the Memorandum or of the agreement was found. Art. VI.3 bounds it: Israel evacuates its outpost at the Cemetery (MR 0816-0723), so that point is inside the line, and new Israeli outposts may be set up at MR 0836-0700, east of it, so the line reaches the frontier south-east of Rafah, between about N 70 and N 72 km. Carrying the highway's bearing on from Gaza reaches the frontier at about MR 077.7-075.6, north of the Cemetery, and is therefore wrong; a 3-km offset of the coast road through Khan Yunis (MR 083.7-084.2) and Rafah (078.1-077.6), carried on its bearing, reaches the frontier near N 73, also north-west of the Cemetery. The Egyptian-held area is not drawn either, since it needs the whole line. From 22 Feb 1950 the line as drawn on the signed modus vivendi map (S/1471) is a separate feature (egypt_mv1950_demarcation), with its zone A and C lines (egypt_mv1950_zone_lines). Art. VI.4: in the Bethlehem-Hebron area no line was demarcated (left to a later agreement); nothing is drawn there.

UN Archives (search.archives.un.org): the catalogue needs a JavaScript check (not passed with a plain HTTP client); no digitised map found through search engines.

Wikimedia Commons (API searches: '1949 armistice map Jordan Israel', 'Jordan Israel armistice agreement map 1949', 'Jerusalem armistice map 1949', 'Jerusalem cease-fire 30 November 1948 map', 'S/1302', 'Green Line 1949 original map'): 'File:Green Line - Cease Fire Agreement 30 Nov 1948.jpg' is a 3119 x 8630 px colour copy of the signed map 1, the same size as UNISPAL's original but not the same file (SHA-1 3d5990f9... against 370af7aa...), uploaded as 'own work' under CC0 with no source: not used, not even as a cross-check (owner ruling); 'File:UN Map of Central Jerusalem November 1949.jpg' is a later UN cartographic map (November 1949), not map 2; the others are later drawings (H212/10/1955, user-made comparisons).
National Library of Israel and ECF ('Original Green Line Map', https://ecf.org.il/media_items/338): not reached with a plain HTTP client in this pass (JavaScript catalogues); to request.
fronts.dating: from 1949-04-03 for sectors (a), (b) (not drawn), (c), (d); line A in the Iraqi sector in stages (Art. VI.3): 1949-05-08, 1949-05-22 and 1949-07-17; until each stage the earlier military line held (not drawn).

partition.why: The lines do not yet enclose the areas each side held: the Egypt line stops at Gaza and the Jordan line leaves out Jerusalem. Until they do, the Mandate sub-district layer stays as the base under them (tools/borders_bake.py), each front's end recorded per front.

properties.name: Armistice Demarcation Line (Lebanon-Israel): the international boundary
properties.accuracy: about +-1 km: the Mandate frontier digitised from the Survey of Palestine 1:750,000 map for the 1948 sub-districts (its uncertain segments, Ras en Naqura and the Metulla tip, to about +-1.5 km); its east end lies 0.55 km from the tripoint of the Syria agreement's Annex I (MR 208.7-294.2).
properties.method: Art. V.1: 'The Armistice Demarcation Line shall follow the international boundary between the Lebanon and Palestine.' The boundary is the 1923 line (boundary pillars), taken as the Mandate frontier already digitised (content/map/subdistricts_1948.geojson), from the coast at Ras en Naqura to the Lebanon-Syria-Palestine tripoint.

properties.name: Armistice Demarcation Line (Syria-Israel)
properties.accuracy: the Annex I points exact; stretches the text calls 'a line' straight between them; the others traced on the annexed map's green line. Evidence, independent of the trace: the map's own 1-km grid fits each sheet at 29 m rms before the points register the scan; where the line is the Demilitarized Zone's edge it agrees with the hatching of the other scan (separately georeferenced) to a median of 12-98 m per stretch. (The points' distance to the green ink after registration, median 34 m, is small by construction and is not evidence.) About +-0.1 km (the MR precision) at the points and +-0.1-0.2 km along the traced stretches, except the two short Lake Hula shoreline stretches, 9-10 and 10-11, only 9% and 18% on green ink (under 1.5 km each; error bounded by their length, about +-0.3 km). Lake Hula's shoreline is the 1949 one (the lake was drained in the 1950s).
properties.method: Annex I's 24 items (typed from UNTS vol. 42 pp. 342-344) converted from the Palestine Grid (EPSG:28191); the stretches between points as below; Art. V.3: the line is as delineated on the map of Annex I.

properties.accuracy: about +-0.3 km: the Wadi Hasi mouth and Deir Suneid read off the 1:100,000 sheet (+-0.1 km; georeference rms 8 m), the highway traced on it (96% of the trace on its red fill) and offset 3 km; the turn at Deir Suneid ('in an easterly direction through Deir Suneid and across the highway') is read as the mouth-Deir Suneid direction carried on to the offset line. properties.name: Demarcation line as drawn on the signed 1950 modus vivendi map (Gaza-Rafah area)
properties.agreement: Modus vivendi to the Egypt-Israel General Armistice Agreement
properties.accuracy: about +-0.1 km: waypoints read on the drawn dash-dot of the signed 1:20,000 sheets every 0.5-1 km and joined straight (georeference rms 20 m; the dash-dot is about 12 m wide; ink within 3 px along 54%, 89%, 54% of each piece); the three points the text puts on the line are exact. The signed map draws the demarcation line only in pieces: on sheet 1 from its south neatline (N 100) to MR 106.95-102.40 (the text's point; north-east of it the dotted line is zone A's); on sheet 2 from MR 90.05-87.11 to 89.07-85.25, and from MR 87.63-77.31 to 82.74-72.61. North of N 102.6 the 1949 line is not redrawn on the map; between N 85.4 and 77.3 zone C lies against it but no demarcation line is drawn; the two sheets do not cover N 90-100; south-west of MR 82.8-72.6 nothing is drawn. Those stretches are not drawn here.
properties.method: The modus vivendi of 22 February 1950 (S/1471) sets local patrol zones A, B and C beside the demarcation line and, by its Art. III, does not change either party's position on the Art. VI.1 line; its signed map draws that line (dash-dot, 'Demarcation line'). Drawn here where the map draws it, through waypoints read off the georeferenced sheets. A later drawing of the 1949 line, kept as its own feature and date.
properties.gaps: The signed map draws the demarcation line only in pieces: on sheet 1 from its south neatline (N 100) to MR 106.95-102.40 (the text's point; north-east of it the dotted line is zone A's); on sheet 2 from MR 90.05-87.11 to 89.07-85.25, and from MR 87.63-77.31 to 82.74-72.61. North of N 102.6 the 1949 line is not redrawn on the map; between N 85.4 and 77.3 zone C lies against it but no demarcation line is drawn; the two sheets do not cover N 90-100; south-west of MR 82.8-72.6 nothing is drawn. Those stretches are not drawn here.

properties.agreement: Hashemite Jordan Kingdom-Israel General Armistice Agreement
properties.accuracy: LOW ACCURACY, about +-1-1.5 km: traced from a low-resolution copy of the signed map 1 (1:250,000; about 51 m a pixel; the pen line is about 5 px, 250 m, wide), georeferenced on town symbols (north sheet leave-one-out rms 0.77 km, max 1.44; south sheet 1.47 km, max 2.61); 94% of the trace on the pen ink. To be replaced from a full-resolution scan.
properties.method: Art. VI.2: line A on map 1 (the sector held by Iraqi forces), traced from the map; dated by Art. VI.3's stages, shown from each deadline (until then the existing military lines held; they are not drawn). Art. VI.3 stages for line A, as read here (the article names areas, not points): (a) 'In the area west of the road from Baqa to Jaljulia, and thence to the east of Kafr Qasim: within five weeks' = line A from Baqa south to Kafr Qasim, by 8 May 1949; (b) 'In the area of Wadi Ara north of the line from Baqa to Zubeiba: within seven weeks' = line A from Zubeiba round Wadi Ara to Baqa, by 22 May 1949; (c) 'In all other areas of the Iraqi sector: within fifteen weeks' = line A east of Zubeiba to the Jordan and from Kafr Qasim to Kh Deir Arab (MR 1510-1574), by 17 July 1949. Split at the trace's points nearest Baqa al-Gharbiyye, Zubeiba (Wikidata 'Zububa') and Kafr Qasim. The dates are deadlines ('within ... weeks'; 'pending which the existing military lines may be maintained'): each stretch is shown from its deadline, a convention; the actual handover dates (May-July 1949) are not researched.
properties.source_quality_note: Traced from the UNISPAL copy of map 1 (3119 x 8630 px); to be replaced from a full-resolution scan.

properties.accuracy: LOW ACCURACY, about +-1-1.5 km: traced from a low-resolution copy of the signed map 1 (1:250,000; about 51 m a pixel; the pen line is about 5 px, 250 m, wide), georeferenced on town symbols (north sheet leave-one-out rms 0.77 km, max 1.44; south sheet 1.47 km, max 2.61); 94% of the trace on the pen ink. To be replaced from a full-resolution scan.
properties.method: Art. VI.2: line A on map 1 (the sector held by Iraqi forces), traced from the map; dated by Art. VI.3's stages, shown from each deadline (until then the existing military lines held; they are not drawn). Art. VI.3 stages for line A, as read here (the article names areas, not points): (a) 'In the area west of the road from Baqa to Jaljulia, and thence to the east of Kafr Qasim: within five weeks' = line A from Baqa south to Kafr Qasim, by 8 May 1949; (b) 'In the area of Wadi Ara north of the line from Baqa to Zubeiba: within seven weeks' = line A from Zubeiba round Wadi Ara to Baqa, by 22 May 1949; (c) 'In all other areas of the Iraqi sector: within fifteen weeks' = line A east of Zubeiba to the Jordan and from Kafr Qasim to Kh Deir Arab (MR 1510-1574), by 17 July 1949. Split at the trace's points nearest Baqa al-Gharbiyye, Zubeiba (Wikidata 'Zububa') and Kafr Qasim. The dates are deadlines ('within ... weeks'; 'pending which the existing military lines may be maintained'): each stretch is shown from its deadline, a convention; the actual handover dates (May-July 1949) are not researched.
properties.source_quality_note: Traced from the UNISPAL copy of map 1 (3119 x 8630 px); to be replaced from a full-resolution scan.
